summary.intent: Review and publish a subagent's perf branch (declared single-flight) that deduplicates concurrent identical `declared` checker requests, verifying the worker's report independently rather than trusting it.
summary.outcome: Branch perf/declared-single-flight was verified (lint, semantic tests, output diffs) and published as PR #513 with the lead's evidence. Loaded-run evidence was added to #511 showing the heap clamp fixes degraded runs (0/24 vs 3/24). A bug in the lead's own degraded-run detector was found.

repo: Degraded semantic runs are signaled by a `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic with severity other than `info`; every run carries a SEMANTIC_BACKEND diagnostic, so its presence alone is not a signal.
The degraded message starts with text like '620 component(s) kept…', so matching the text 'semantic backend' does not detect it.

Single-flight `BatchAnswers` in `asked.rs` is used by descriptions, tags, symbols and parents in `declared.rs`; it keeps one batch per call and cannot form a wait cycle because callers send held requests before waiting and failed askers release their slot.
Chakra getSymbolOfDeclarationForChecker calls drop from 7,626 to 2,552 with the change; Mantine has no overlap (480 vs 505). The win is fewer duplicate checker requests, not CPU/RSS or wall time.
Spectrum output varies run to run, probably because of private-name ids (issue #512), not confirmed.
Chakra runs degrade under load on main (3/24 at load average 75-95) and 0/24 with the heap clamp from #511.
workflow: Independently re-verify a subagent's hand-back (rebuild release binary, rerun lint/tests, diff outputs across repo corpora) before publishing; this exposed a determinism issue and a detector bug.
Run determinism checks several times per binary, since single runs miss intermittent degradation.
Validate a diagnostic detector against a known-degraded run before relying on it for claims.

friction: The lead's degraded-run detector was broken (matched wrong text), which weakened the batch comparison and #510's 'no run carried a fallback' claim.
Chakra output varied across runs on both the new binary and main, requiring extra investigation.
Several helper scripts (spec2.py was written twice) and detector fixes required multiple iterations.
Heavy machine load (average 75-95) made measurements noisy.
open_items: #510 body (already merged) still contains the claim based on the broken detector and has not been corrected.
`gate_harness` and wall-clock measurements were not run for #513; CI is expected to cover gate_harness.
Spectrum's occasional differing output is unconfirmed as #512's private-name id bug.
Chakra degraded runs (~3.3k batches) on base were not investigated by the worker, and the heap clamp fix in #511 is not yet merged.
Convert-memo single-flight and early-session reuse subagent work is still in progress and needs the same review.
